topic: Revising a group argument rather than polishing its language
grammarFocus: 学术论证的限定、因果、对比与证据范围
title: Revising a group argument rather than polishing its language
instructions: 原创学术微训练；场景、机构与数值均为虚构模拟，不是事实报道或官方试题。先独立盲听答题，再用原句核对限定、比较与因果。短篇专项不能替代完整陌生测评。
transcript:
Tutor: Your group presentation is clearly spoken, but its conclusion goes beyond the evidence.
Jon: We said remote meetings improve participation. Our survey showed that more people attended after the meetings moved online.
Tutor: Attendance is one part of participation. Did you measure who contributed to discussion?
Jon: We counted contributions in two recordings. A few participants spoke much more than the others. We should distinguish presence from speaking opportunities.
Tutor: What else changed at the same time?
Jon: Meetings moved from eight in the morning to lunchtime. The new time could explain some of the attendance increase.
Tutor: Exactly. Can your design separate the effects of timing and format?
Jon: Not with the existing comparison. We can describe the combined change, but we cannot attribute the whole increase to the online format.
Tutor: What revision would make the conclusion defensible?
Jon: We will say that attendance rose after both changes, while discussion remained uneven in the two sessions we examined. Then we will propose a further comparison using the same meeting time.
Tutor: Will you remove the participants' comments?
Jon: No. We will keep them as examples of experience, with permission, rather than claiming they represent everyone. The revised draft will be ready on Thursday.

questions.prompt: What additional aspect of participation was examined?
options: The speed of the internet connection.
questions.explanation: 依据原文“We counted contributions in two recordings.”。正确项保持了原文的范围和关系，其余项改动了该信息。

questions.prompt: What distinction does Jon now recognise?
options: Attendance is unrelated to participation in any sense.
A recording measures every aspect of experience.
Being present differs from having speaking opportunities.
answers: Being present differs from having speaking opportunities.
questions.explanation: 依据原文“distinguish presence from speaking opportunities.”。正确项保持了原文的范围和关系，其余项改动了该信息。

questions.prompt: To what part of the day were meetings moved?
questions.explanation: 依据原文“to lunchtime.”。答案按原文填写，保留限定范围。

questions.prompt: What can the existing design establish?
options: Attendance rose after a combination of changes.
The format alone caused the entire increase.
The meeting time alone caused the entire increase.
answers: Attendance rose after a combination of changes.
questions.explanation: 依据原文“describe the combined change”。正确项保持了原文的范围和关系，其余项改动了该信息。

questions.prompt: What will be held constant in the proposed further comparison?
questions.explanation: 依据原文“the same meeting time.”。答案按原文填写，保留限定范围。

questions.prompt: How will personal comments be used?
options: As replacements for all attendance records.
As permitted examples rather than universal evidence.
As proof of every participant’s opinion.
answers: As permitted examples rather than universal evidence.
questions.explanation: 依据原文“as examples of experience, with permission”。正确项保持了原文的范围和关系，其余项改动了该信息。
questions.evidence: as examples of experience, with permission

questions.explanation: 依据原文“on Thursday.”。答案按原文填写，保留限定范围。

grammar.title: 结论强度与情态动词
grammar.explanation: may/could 表示可能；must 表示这里给出的强制规则。根据句中明确说明的证据或规则作答，不把小样本可能性改成普遍必然。
grammar.example: The new time could explain some of the attendance increase.

questions.prompt: The effect _____ vary; the sample is too small to be certain. （只填空白，保持其余文字不变）
questions.explanation: may/could 表示可能；must 表示这里给出的强制规则。根据句中明确说明的证据或规则作答，不把小样本可能性改成普遍必然。 本句为：The effect may vary; the sample is too small to be certain.
questions.evidence: The effect may vary; the sample is too small to be certain.
